Probability maps · Final candidate weights · Method and scope · Evidence

Given a release cell in R, estimate the historical distribution of the observed future endpoint. The maps compare a forecast fitted without the displayed holdout IDs with endpoints from those same held-out IDs.

30-day all-fold result (Analytic blend): blending increases the held-out hit rate of the nominal 90% probability set from 67.20% to 86.20%, while its mean geographic size increases from 64.9 to 128.4 cells. Wider coverage has a cost in concentration.

These weights were selected using all-development base out-of-fold predictions, then the bases were refitted on all development data. Their tuning score is not an independent evaluation. The maps above use each outer fold's independently tuned weight, so its displayed lambda can differ.

Method and scope

Empirical conditional endpoint model: P_B2(j | i,h) = N_ij(h) / Σ_k N_ik(h). Here i is the origin cell, j the destination, h the horizon and N the eligible training-pair count. For a complete forecast, Brier = 1 − 2p_j + Σ_k p_k², with j the observed destination.

  • B0: persistence in the origin cell. B1: endpoint frequencies pooled across R. B2: endpoint frequencies conditional on the origin cell.
  • Optimization: compare a 0.1-step lambda grid with the continuous minimum of the same quadratic Brier objective. Five outer and four inner whole-ID folds separate evaluation from weight selection. All eligible hourly pairs have equal weight.
  • Reading the results: smaller Brier is better; it is not percentage accuracy. Set hit rate, forecast availability and region size answer different questions. Raw zero probabilities remain visible and give infinite log loss.
  • Limits: these are nonseasonal, pooled, historical drifter endpoint forecasts at 7 and 30 days. The release prior follows sampled positions inside each cell. Annual, seasonal, grounding and object-specific performance are not validated here. The paired bootstrap is conditional on saved OOF predictions and does not repeat training.

Next research checkpoints

Investigate residual zero-probability outcomes and calibration; then test justified seasonal and longer-horizon extensions. These are planned comparisons, not demonstrated capabilities.
